item.text:
<linkedin_post>Google is testing whether AI chips can do useful work in orbit, starting with a satellite that carries four of its TPUs. The prototype is online and has run a preloaded Gemma model, though its power supply limits it to one chip for about 20 minutes at a time.

The next question is how reliably the hardware works in space. Radiation can flip bits in memory and corrupt data without triggering typical monitoring tools. Google’s ground tests suggested inference would be less affected than model training; the satellite will let engineers measure the effects in orbit.

Google plans to follow with two higher-power satellites in 2027 if the chips perform well. Those spacecraft would test optical links designed to let satellites share processing work.</linkedin_post>
